text:
Anna: customer on Private reported pip/docker/model pulls failing after they enabled corporate TLS-inspecting proxy. errors are CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED and hostname mismatch.

Anna: example from their node bootstrap: 
```
Collecting redwood-client
  Could not fetch URL https://files.pythonhosted.org/... (certificate verify failed)
requests.exceptions.SSLError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed (_ssl.c:XXXX)
curl: (60) SSL: certificate subject name 'corp-proxy.corp' does not match target 'auth.redwood.ai'
```

Marta: sounds like MITM proxy replacing certs. ask infra: are they doing explicit tls intercept or passthrough? need SNI passthrough for our hosts. please run these and paste results:
```
dig +short auth.redwood.ai
openssl s_client -connect auth.redwood.ai:443 -servername auth.redwood.ai | sed -n '1,60p'
curl -v https://auth.redwood.ai/health 2>&1 | sed -n '1,80p'
```

Anna: infra replied: it's an intercepting proxy, corporate mandate. they only allow exceptions by hostname list. they can also add internal certs to trust stores but prefer allowlist.

Chris: short-term ask: they need SNI/TLS passthrough (no cert substitution) for these hostnames on 443:
- auth.redwood.ai
- telemetry.redwood-inference.com
- model-registry.redwood.ai
- packages.redwood-inference.com
- files.pythonhosted.org
- pypi.org
- registry-1.docker.io
- api.github.com
- npmjs.org
Also include any private registry hostnames they use for model artifacts.

Chris: note: our edges are behind CDNs/load balancers so IPs change. allowlist by hostname/SNI is strongly preferred. if they absolutely need CIDRs, we'll open an engineering ticket to provide a maintained list.

Anna: customer tried adding auth.redwood.ai to proxy exceptions but pip still fails because pip pulls from files.pythonhosted.org and mirrors. they also have conda and apt in play.

Marta: ask for repro with verbose package client output. e.g., `pip install --no-cache-dir -v redwood-client` and `docker pull --debug <image>` and paste. Also capture `curl --resolve auth.redwood.ai:443:<edge-ip> https://auth.redwood.ai/health` using an edge IP from `dig` to see where TLS breaks.

Anna: customer posted curl output: 
```
$ curl -v https://auth.redwood.ai/health
* Connected to proxy.corp (10.10.10.5) port 443 (#0)
* SSL certificate problem: certificate is not yet valid
* Closing connection 0
```

Chris: classic proxy cert substitution. If customer cannot do passthrough, alternatives:
- Add our public hostnames to proxy passthrough list (recommended).
- Or, have them install their proxy CA into the node trust store *and* configure the proxy to preserve original hostname in cert subject/SANs (rare).
- For short-lived bootstrap failure, we can provide a script that fetches model artifacts via an out-of-band trusted location if infra allows a one-time exception.

Kevin: I'll create an internal ticket to generate a published egress CIDR set for Private customers. won't be immediate. tag: @kevin. ops-bot will track.

ops-bot: Support ticket #SUP-19721 created for CIDR publication. Assignee: Kevin. Priority: P2.

Marta: runbook update suggestion:
- Default guidance: allowlist by SNI/hostname for ports 443 (and 80 where relevant).
- Include python/npm/docker/apt/yum hostnames in default list.
- If streaming APIs used, ensure ALPN/h2 passthrough (some proxies downgrade ALPN which breaks long-lived streams).
- If customer insists on MITM, document the required cert characteristics and client trust steps.

Anna: customer will test adding the full hostname list as exceptions (including files.pythonhosted.org and registry-1.docker.io) and report back Monday. I'll collect verbose logs if it still fails.

Chris: one extra note: some corporate proxies rewrite SNI to a single gateway host. if that is the case, even hostname allowlist won't help. ask them to confirm that SNI values are preserved by the proxy. `openssl s_client` with `-servername` is the quickest check.

Marta: also ask whether they use transparent proxying at network edge vs explicit proxy config on hosts. transparent intercept is harder to carve exceptions for.

Anna: thanks all, closing until we have repro logs or they confirm passthrough works. will reopen if needed :thumbsup:
